# Software is communication

## Defaults are advice

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- [EpiNow2](https://epiforecasts.io/EpiNow2/) has been on CRAN since
  1 September 2020
- CDC used it for nowcasts and $R_t$
- Every argument a user leaves alone is a decision they inherited from
  us. The generation time, the delays, the prior on $R_t$, the sampler
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
```r
estimates <- epinow(
  data = reported_cases,
  generation_time = gt_opts(example_generation_time),
  delays = delay_opts(example_incubation_period + reporting_delay),
  rt = rt_opts(prior = LogNormal(mean = 2, sd = 0.2)),
  stan = stan_opts(cores = 4)
)
```

::: {.attribution}
[EpiNow2 vignette](https://epiforecasts.io/EpiNow2/articles/EpiNow2.html) ·
[CRAN archive](https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/EpiNow2/),
1.1.0 dated 2020-09-01 ·
[CDC CFA, Behind the model: nowcasting](https://www.cdc.gov/cfa-behind-the-model/php/data-research/nowcasting.html),
updated 2026-01-30 ·
[MMWR 73(46), 2024-11-21](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/73/wr/mm7346a3.htm)
:::
:::
::::

## The limits travel less well than the method

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The estimates went out as CSV files on GitHub
- They were used in publications by people who did not interact with us
- The limitations sat on a methods page that 20,000 of 1.2 million page
  views reached

> Of course this can cause issues if the limitations of the method are
> poorly communicated.
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}

## Community as the channel

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- [epinowcast](https://www.epinowcast.org/). Over 50 researchers and
  public health analysts
- 31 seminars from May 2023 to May 2026
- By 2026 my own verdict was that in many cases the package is too complex
  for anyone else to use

> Trying to build a community of practice as community >> methods or
> models alone.
:::

## Evaluation as communication

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- [scoringutils](https://epiforecasts.io/scoringutils/) scores
  probabilistic forecasts. WIS is the hubs' headline measure
- Raw scores are not comparable when teams miss weeks
- Pairwise comparison on the overlapping forecasts gives a relative skill
  each team can read
- UKHSA, the UK Health Security Agency, asked us for guidance on
  evaluation
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-pairwise-illustration.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Three models compared in pairs to give a relative skill score"}

::: {.attribution}
Figure from the
[scoringutils manuscript](https://github.com/epiforecasts/scoringutils/tree/main/inst/manuscript),
